title: Double arrows : logs
body:
@MilosKozak You had asked the logs when double arrows arrive in AAPS.

I think they happen when there is a steep direction change in BGs. This night's examples : sensor compression, goes low, I turn or wake up with the alerts and BGs raise. I have the last dev and am using average smoothing. G6 and xDrip.

Arrows are OK in xDrip

![Screenshot_20241221_032207_xDrip+.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2f49f46-0598-4f38-b3ea-4be813ddd4f6)

![Screenshot_20241221_032217_AAPS.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bd01a54-b2cc-4e2a-958c-cc6c837a963a)

![Screenshot_20241221_032230_AAPS.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/384be197-a529-49bd-8c01-c6fc2db0abcd)

The logs during the double arrows (look around 03:17 

![AndroidAPS_LOG_during.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18217983/AndroidAPS_LOG_during.zip)

And a bit after the double arrows

![AndroidAPS_LOG_after.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18217988/AndroidAPS_LOG_after.zip)

An automation kicks in in case of steep drop.

xdrip is sending DoubleDown. AAPS doesn't change the arrow if provided.
Report to xDrip

Ok, tnx. It's funny how they send double down arrows but show only one up...

Please leave this issue open. I'll link it to them.

i don't think we should have different behavior for diffrent BG sources.
xDrip should decide what should be presented to AAPS
Navid from xDrip isn't interrested in changing anything and thinks that the double arrows come from the transmitter itself. I don't use BYODA and I can’t check if it's the case.
